verdict.text: The before read in release-tag.yml now uses `scripts/release.py manifest`, which reads apm/apm.yml alone, so a before commit whose root apm.yml differs or is missing still yields its version and a lowered version is still caught.
`current` keeps its copy check and is built on the new `manifest_version`.
The summary ack was the right call.
The plan's intent is met with no regressions.
Ran `loopctl gate stamp` in the worktree: lint, format, tests, integration, eval rows r1 and r2 all pass, stamp green dae2c155c401b25fe5e691536e207315557f7a7af37214b79cd6ad8e392971f5.
Ran r1 by hand too: 5 passed.
r1: test_release.py checks that `manifest` prints 0.3.0 when the root apm.yml says 0.2.9 and also when it is deleted, and that it exits 1 with no stdout when apm/apm.yml is gone.

test_workflows.py pulls the real `OLD=` line out of release-tag.yml, rejects `current`, and runs that line in bash against a before folder whose copies disagree, then checks that `compare` says lowered.
If the workflow went back to `current || true`, OLD would be empty and the test would fail, so it covers fails_when.
Read the whole diff: release.py's docstring, usage, argparse wiring and `--repo` handling; `_apm_version` returns None for a missing file, so `manifest` refuses with the same message either way.
Consistency: ADR 0013's "current refuses when a copy differs" is still true.
The overview's diagram and release-tag bullet now name `manifest` correctly.
Summary ack: .okf/summary.md says nothing about release.py subcommands or how release-tag reads versions; it only links ADR 0012.
The overview edit leaves every claim in the summary true, so recording `checked` against architecture/overview is right.
Rewriting the summary would have been wrong.
